title: Interpreting antiretroviral exposure and drug-drug interactions in pregnancy: A clinically anchored framework for HIV pharmacology.
what: In pregnancy, antiretroviral drug-drug interactions must be interpreted against dynamic changes in gastrointestinal physiology, plasma-protein binding, renal elimination, hepatic enzyme activity and membrane transporter expression. Interaction studies quantify geometric mean exposure ratios relative to nonpregnant adults, but these measures describe relative pharmacokinetic change rather than whether effective exposure is preserved.
source: PubMed, British journal of clinical pharmacology
original_title: Interpreting antiretroviral exposure and drug-drug interactions in pregnancy: A clinically anchored framework for HIV pharmacology.

title: From CYP450 pharmacogenomics to personalized medicine: clinical evidence, dosing guidelines, and future perspectives.
what: Interindividual variability in drug response remains a critical challenge in contemporary pharmacotherapy, and cytochrome P450 (CYP450) genetic polymorphisms are a principal determinant of this heterogeneity. The CYP450 superfamily mediates the oxidative biotransformation of 70-80% of clinically prescribed medications.
original_title: From CYP450 pharmacogenomics to personalized medicine: clinical evidence, dosing guidelines, and future perspectives.
